description:
The heap runs a second collector inside the first. Objects larger than the last SIZE_TABLE entry (~6 MiB) are allocated as system-allocator fragments (heap/fragment.rs) and collected by mark-sweep: a mark bit, classify_fragment on every forwarded pointer, a two-queue mixed-mode BFS in gc_with_extra_roots, a sweep, fragment ranges in every address-membership test, a fragment split in the gift window, GiftSegment.fragments, fragment_survivors and fragment_live_bytes in GcStats, and fragment bytes in the collect-now predicate. All of it exists because the size table clamps at 32 entries.

BEAM has no such thing on the process heap. Its size table runs to the address space (heap_sizes in erl_gc.c grows Fibonacci then 20 percent until max_heap_size) and a large term is copied like any other. Binaries over 64 bytes are already off-heap here (SHARED_BIN_THRESHOLD_BYTES), so a fragment only ever held a struct or map above 6 MiB.

Done when:
- pick_size_class never clamps. Classes within the table are pooled as today; a block above the table is allocated exactly (rounded to 16) and released to the allocator, not the pool. Block carries what it needs to free itself either way.
- fragment.rs is deleted: Fragment, CopiedObject's fragment role, classify_fragment, mark_fragment_for_tracing, FRAGMENT_THRESHOLD. gc_with_extra_roots has one scan loop over to-space. The fragments field, fragment_bytes, the fragment term in should_gc, the fragment split in begin_gift/end_gift, GiftSegment.fragments and fragment_count, the fragment ranges in the address iterator, the fragment free in Drop for Heap and Drop for GiftSegment, and GcStats.fragment_survivors / fragment_live_bytes are gone. GcStats.live_bytes is the to-space fill.
- The fragment tests in heap_test.rs (alloc_oversized_routes_to_fragment_list, rooted_fragment_survives_gc, unrooted_fragment_is_freed_by_gc, mixed_fragment_liveness, fragment_to_fragment_edge_survives_gc, fragment_to_block_edge_promotes_block_object, heap_drop_releases_fragments_without_leak) and the two in gift_test.rs (a_gift_with_an_oversize_object_travels_as_a_fragment_and_is_marked_not_copied, dropping_an_ungrafted_segment_returns_its_blocks_frees_its_fragments_and_releases_its_stubs) are replaced by tests of the new fact: an object above the old threshold allocates into an exact block, survives a collection by being copied (its address changes, to_space_capacity_bytes >= its size), is freed when unrooted, and a gift carrying one grafts and collects.
- Any .agent/docs or guide sentence describing fragments or the 6 MiB limit is rewritten to the present fact.
- Full gate green. Commit in Why / What changed / Verification form. No co-author trailer.

Tests: as listed in the third bullet. Each must be shown to exercise the above-table path (assert the block is not pooled: pool_outstanding_blocks unchanged across its allocation).
Documentation in the same commit: every .agent/docs page, guide (guides/*.html), README.md section and fixture README that describes a mechanism this ticket changes or removes is rewritten to the present fact in the same commit, and a grep for the old names and phrases over .agent, guides, README.md and fixtures returns nothing. If a worked example in a guide or a numbered fixture illustrates the old behaviour, it is updated or replaced in the same commit. The close-out ticket (.13) is a final sweep, not the place where documentation first happens.
title: The size table has no ceiling and oversize objects are copied like any other
